title: Priority Waterline and Tenant De-escalation PRD (draft)
content:
Context:
We keep building richer burst and tenant-isolation primitives for Dedicated. Most designs focus on either strict reservation semantics (hard isolation) or elastic burst fabrics (credits, warm pools). Operators and platform customers ask for a middle ground: a predictable way to preserve SLOs for high-priority tenants while allowing lower-tier customers to continue useful throughput under load rather than hard-cut them off.

Proposal (sketch): Priority Waterline = per-tenant adaptive threshold that determines when the system begins progressive de-escalation.
- Waterline is expressed in two axes: latency headroom (quantile-based) and compute occupancy (vCPU/GPU slot util).
- It is dynamic: moves with observed 95th/99th latency and pool occupancy; we anchor it to SLOs and a safety margin.
- When a tenant crosses its waterline, we run a de-escalation ladder rather than immediate eviction.

De-escalation ladder (example steps, incremental):
1) Soft rate-limit (token-bucket throttle to reduce incoming QPS by X%).
2) Swap to lower-fidelity model variant (quantized or smaller model) if permitted by tenant policy.
3) Disable non-critical features (long-context, streaming or heavy tools) for requests flagged as opportunistic.
4) Temporary micro-slab (move to an opportunistic pool with lower SLO guarantees) with soft-fallback to hosted.
5) Eviction/queue (last resort) with restart window and grace notifications.

Key behaviors and rules:
- Priority tiers: platinum/gold/silver/baseline. Each tier has configured waterline aggressiveness and permitted de-escalations.
- Credits & burst interaction: tenants can have burst credits; consuming credits raises their waterline tolerance temporarily. Credits decay over time.
- Preemption rules: higher-priority tenants may preempt lower-tier opportunistic micro-slabs but not tenants with same priority within a pool.
- Safety fence: absolute minimum capacity per physical node (avoid complete starvation).

Autoscaling integration:
- Autoscaler should be waterline-aware. When waterlines are frequently triggered across pools, scale-up earlier than naive CPU/GPU utilization triggers because it's an SLO-risk signal.
- Scale-down needs hysteresis: do not scale down if any tenant recently hit a waterline within the cooldown window.
- Warm-pool policy: maintain micro-warm slots reserved for high-tier tenants to reduce latency bloat when waterlines move.

Burst options and economics:
- Two credit currencies: (a) instantaneous burst credits (fast to spend, fast decay), (b) reserve credits (allocated monthly, decays slowly).
- Pricing model: credits for burst are billable; mixing commit tiers with credits gives headroom flexibility.
- Soft-credits: promotional credits that can be consumed but only permit lower-latency-preserving de-escalations, not prevent eviction.

Isolation controls and admin UX:
- Tenant policy config: tier, allowed de-escalations (binary flags), credit pools, waterline sensitivity slider (0.5–2.0 multiplier).
- Admin console: per-pool heatmap showing tenants near waterline, recent triggers, and recommended mitigations (scale, increase credits, change tier).
- Audit logs: every de-escalation step emits structured event (tenant, step, reason, metrics snapshot, action taken).

Observability and SLOs:
- Metrics to expose: waterline position, triggers per-minute, de-escalation step counts, average time to recover to below-waterline, per-tenant P99 latency pre/post de-escalation.
- Alerts: escalate if a tenant hits >3 de-escalations in 10 minutes or if >20% of tenants in a pool hit waterline simultaneously.
- Evaluations: add smoke evals that simulate sudden QPS jumps to validate ladder correctness and automations.

Rollout plan (incremental):
- Phase 0: telemetry & dry-run mode. Compute waterline and show predictions in console; do not act.
- Phase 1: soft de-escalation (rate-limits + feature flags) for internal tenants only.
- Phase 2: expand to low-risk external tenants; enable credit consumption path.
- Phase 3: full release with policy UI and autoscaler integration.

Operational runbook (ops notes):
- If a high-tier tenant repeatedly hits waterline -> recommend dedicated pool or increase credits/commit.
- If multiple tenants in a pool hit waterline -> consider emergency scale-up or divert opportunistic tenants to overflow pools.
- Debugging: capture KV cache pressure, batching time, kernel contention metrics at trigger time.

Open questions / risks:
- How to avoid tenants gaming the waterline (burst-credit gaming)? Consider cooldown windows and anti-abuse heuristics.
- Interaction with private deployments (customer-managed autoscalers) — need local config vs control-plane defaults.
- UX complexity: how many knobs before customers are confused? Start with conservative defaults and a simple slider.
- Billing edge cases when de-escalation changes model fidelity mid-request.

Action items / next steps (TODOs):
- [ ] Align on canonical metric definitions (waterline latency formula). (Owner: Liam)
- [ ] Prototype dry-run dashboard and per-tenant simulation. (Owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Spike: autoscaler hook that raises priority-based scale-up. (Owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Draft UI wireframes for policy config + recommended defaults. (Owner: Asha)
- [ ] Draft e2e test harness that simulates 50x burst on pool. (Owner: Eng Reliability)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally permissive at the moment — want feedback on the ladder ordering and which steps are too heavy-handed.
- Priorities: protect P99 latency for platinum tenants while avoiding brittle full-eviction for medium tiers.
- Feel free to add examples of threshold numbers (I left those as TBD until we align on metric shape).

Quick sketches / examples (for discussion):
- Platinum: waterline = max( SLO * 0.9, 95th historical * 1.05 ). De-escalation: 1->2->3 only; eviction disabled.
- Silver: waterline = max( SLO * 0.75, 95th hist * 1.2 ). De-escalation: 1->2->3->4. Eviction allowed as last resort.

Slack refs: #dedicated-autoscale, #ops-incident for prior episodes where pools saw correlated latency spikes.

End.
